env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

# Trigger: LoGOs sources with no module marker. Plain go meets
# main.lgo and re-executes as logos.
cd nomark
go run .
stdout '^auto-detect$'
go build -o $WORK/nomark$GOEXE .
exec $WORK/nomark$GOEXE
stdout '^auto-detect$'
go list all
stdout 'example\.com/nomark'
go build -o $WORK/nomarkx$GOEXE .
exec $WORK/nomarkx$GOEXE
stdout '^auto-detect$'

# A LoGOs-only flag does not block source detection: it reaches the
# directory check before the flag parser can reject it.
go build -pedantic -o $WORK/nomark-ped$GOEXE .
exec $WORK/nomark-ped$GOEXE
stdout '^auto-detect$'
go build -json-diagnostics -o $WORK/nomark-json$GOEXE .
exec $WORK/nomark-json$GOEXE
stdout '^auto-detect$'

# Trigger: a ./... walk meets the LoGOs directory, which plain go
# would skip silently.
cd nomark
go list ./...
stdout 'example\.com/nomark'
cd ..

# Trigger: the module marker. logos.toml beside go.mod re-executes
# before any package loads, so the .lgo test runs under go test.
# The marker fires before the builder starts: one WORK line proves
# the re-execution happened exactly once.
cd marked
go build -x -o $WORK/markedx$GOEXE .
stderr -count=1 '(?m)^WORK='
exec $WORK/markedx$GOEXE
stdout '^marked$'
go test ./...
stdout '^ok\s+example\.com/marked/sub'
go test ./... -test.v
stdout '=== RUN   TestHello'
stdout '--- PASS: TestHello'
cd ..

# Trigger: a LoGOs-only subcommand.
cd marked
go lint ./...
! stderr .
! stdout .
# Toolchain selection does not bypass detection: even a GOTOOLCHAIN naming
# an unavailable stock release re-executes before any switch.
env GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.999.0
go lint ./...
! stderr .
! stdout .
go help lint
stdout '^usage: logos lint'
! stderr .
go build -o $WORK/marked-tc$GOEXE .
exec $WORK/marked-tc$GOEXE
stdout '^marked$'
# In logos mode the command never switches to a stock toolchain.
logos build -o $WORK/marked-tc-logos$GOEXE .
exec $WORK/marked-tc-logos$GOEXE
stdout '^marked$'
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local
cd ..

# Trigger: a Go package importing a LoGOs package of its workspace.
# Each module keeps one kind, so the logos build succeeds.
cd ws/g
go build ./...
go run .
stdout '^from-logos$'
go fmt -n main.go
stdout 'gofmt'
cd ../..

# At an unmarked workspace root outside every member, a ...-style pattern
# unions the members instead of rejecting the prefix.
cd ws
go build ./...
cd ..

# Excluded commands keep upstream text inside a LoGOs module.
cd marked
go version
stdout '^go version go'
go env GOROOT
cp stdout $WORK/go-goroot.txt
logos env GOROOT
cp stdout $WORK/logos-goroot.txt
cmp $WORK/go-goroot.txt $WORK/logos-goroot.txt
go fmt ./...
! stderr 'unknown command'
go help lint
stdout '^usage: logos lint'
! stderr .
cd ..

# A pure Go module is untouched.
cd pure
go run .
stdout '^pure-go$'
go version
stdout '^go version go'
go env GOROOT
! stderr .
# A LoGOs-only flag with no marker or source trigger stays an upstream error.
! go build -pedantic .
stderr 'flag provided but not defined'
cd ..

# The standard library still builds inside a LoGOs module.
cd marked
go build fmt
go list fmt
stdout '^fmt$'
cd ..

# A Go module that depends on a LoGOs module served by a file proxy.
# Plain go finds the module but no Go package in it, and re-executes.
go run genproxy.go $WORK/proxy
cd dep
env GOPROXY=file://$WORK/proxy
env GOSUMDB=off
go get example.com/l/lib
go mod tidy
go build ./...
go run .
stdout '^from-logos$'
cd ..

# An -overlay file that adds a marked member is honored: the overlaid
# marker re-executes and the logos cgo policy denies the build.
cd ov
[cgo] ! go build -overlay=overlay-add.json -o $WORK/ov-m$GOEXE ./m/sub
[cgo] stderr 'cgo_usage'
! logos build -overlay=overlay-add.json -o $WORK/ov-m-logos$GOEXE ./m/sub
stderr 'cgo_usage'
# Without the overlay the disk workspace is unmarked and plain go builds.
[cgo] go build -o $WORK/ov-m-plain$GOEXE ./m/sub
cd ..

# Removing a marked member through the overlay removes the marker: the
# build runs as plain go, with no logos experiment suffix.
cd ovrm
go build -overlay=overlay-rm.json -o $WORK/ovrm-g$GOEXE ./g
go version -m $WORK/ovrm-g$GOEXE
! stdout 'logosarena'
cd ..

# A module needing a newer Go reports the upstream message under both
# spellings.
cd toonew
! go build .
stderr 'go\.mod requires go >= 9\.99'
! logos build .
stderr 'go\.mod requires go >= 9\.99'
cd ..

# A directory-triggered build agrees with an explicit logos build: the
# startup environment applies, not the injected plain defaults.
cd cpu
env GOARCH=amd64
env CGO_ENABLED=0
env GOAMD64=
go build -o $WORK/cpu-go$GOEXE .
go version -m $WORK/cpu-go$GOEXE
stdout 'GOAMD64=v3'
logos build -o $WORK/cpu-logos$GOEXE .
go version -m $WORK/cpu-logos$GOEXE
stdout 'GOAMD64=v3'
env GOARCH=
env CGO_ENABLED=
env GOAMD64=
cd ..

# The directory trigger fires before the builder starts: one WORK line
# proves the re-execution happened exactly once.
cd nomark
go build -x -o $WORK/nomark-x$GOEXE .
stderr -count=1 '(?m)^WORK='
exec $WORK/nomark-x$GOEXE
stdout '^auto-detect$'
cd ..

# In an unmarked cgo module both spellings deny cgo by policy.
cd cgounmarked
env CGO_ENABLED=
[cgo] ! go build -o $WORK/cgounmarked-go$GOEXE .
[cgo] stderr 'cgo_usage'
! logos build -o $WORK/cgounmarked-logos$GOEXE .
stderr 'cgo_usage'
cd ..

-- dep/go.mod --
module example.com/g

go 1.27

-- dep/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/l/lib"
)

func main() { fmt.Println(lib.Msg()) }

-- genproxy.go --
// Copyright 2026 The Go Authors. All rights reserved.
// Use of this source code is governed by a BSD-style
// license that can be found in the LICENSE file.

package main

import (
	"archive/zip"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
)

func writeFile(path, body string) {
	if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(body), 0o666); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

func writeModule(proxy, path, version string, files map[string]string) {
	dir := filepath.Join(proxy, path, "@v")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o777); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	writeFile(filepath.Join(dir, version+".info"), `{"Version":"`+version+`"}`)
	writeFile(filepath.Join(dir, "list"), version+"\n")
	mod := "module " + path + "\n\ngo 1.27\n"
	writeFile(filepath.Join(dir, version+".mod"), mod)
	zf, err := os.Create(filepath.Join(dir, version+".zip"))
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	w := zip.NewWriter(zf)
	add := func(entry, content string) {
		f, err := w.Create(entry)
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		if _, err := f.Write([]byte(content)); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
	}
	for name, content := range files {
		add(path+"@"+version+"/"+name, content)
	}
	add(path+"@"+version+"/go.mod", mod)
	if err := w.Close(); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	if err := zf.Close(); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	fmt.Println("wrote", path, version)
}

func main() {
	proxy := os.Args[1]
	writeModule(proxy, "example.com/l", "v1.0.0", map[string]string{
		"lib/lib.lgo": "package lib\n\nfunc Msg() string { return \"from-logos\" }\n",
	})
}

-- marked/go.mod --
module example.com/marked

go 1.27

-- marked/logos.toml --
[project]

-- marked/main.lgo --
package main

import "fmt"

func hello() string {
	return "marked"
}

func main() {
	fmt.Println(hello())
}

-- marked/sub/sub.lgo --
package sub

func Hello() string {
	return "marked sub"
}

-- marked/sub/sub_test.lgo --
package sub

import "testing"

func TestHello(t *testing.T) {
	if got := Hello(); got != "marked sub" {
		t.Fatalf("Hello() = %q", got)
	}
}
